title: Interview rapport & signal log — Tobin Reyes
action_items: Follow up with candidate on KV-cache tradeoffs example (ask for a small written sketch)
Send short take-home micro-problem: design a 2-tier routing policy for latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive tenants
Share this note with Maya and ask for a quick gut-check ahead of committee call
content:
Purpose: quick, messy capture of human signals that won’t show up on the formal scorecard. I want a separate ledger for rapport, ambiguity-handling, and execution signals — things to reference in the hiring committee and for onboarding risk planning.

Context: interview loop for Sr Runtime Engineer (inference optimizations). Candidate: private repo experience, 6+ yrs infra/ML serving. Came across via referral. Panel: me (Tobin), Maya (runtime infra), Evelyn (SRE). 75-minute loop, mixed design + debugging + culture.

Top-level impressions (raw):
- Calm and conversational; good at explaining constraints in plain English (positive for eng-lead interactions).
- Shows practical tradeoff intuition (latency vs cost) but a bit conservative — prefers safe incremental improvements over aggressive rewrites.
- Can sketch systems quickly but examples tended to default to batch processing mental model; less confident on tight real-time KV-cache evictions and per-request pipelining.

Signals to call out (green / yellow / red):
- Green: communication clarity, ownership anecdotes (ran a migration for a model-serving fleet, had rollout metrics and rollback story).
- Yellow: limited exposure to large-scale continuous batching optimizations and custom CUDA kernels; claims familiarity but could not name specific kernel optimizations beyond mixed-precision and quantization.
- Red: struggled with on-the-fly fallback policies under degraded GPU capacity — initial answer was high-level, had to be prompted three times to propose concrete fallback ordering and data consistency tradeoffs.

Examples they gave I liked:
1) Migration story: moved a light-serving endpoint from single-host to multi-tenant pool; used affinity to reduce cold starts. Named metrics (p95 latency, tail latency increases) and concrete rollback threshold (p95 + 15%). Good ops sense.
2) Heuristic batching: suggested dynamic batch windows based on queue length + token budget — nice, pragmatic. Missing: how to implement without stalling latency SLOs when load is sparse.

Behavioral notes (rapport):
- Positive: asked constructive clarifying questions instead of answering immediately — indicates collaborative posture.
- Slightly negative: when challenged on a kernel-level claim, defensive tone for ~30s then rapidly corrected — not a dealbreaker but worth flag.

Risk & ramp plan (if hired):
- Short-term (0–30d): pair with Maya on a production incident postmortem to learn our batching and cache behavior. Task: write a short doc that maps request shapes -> routing policy.
- Mid-term (30–90d): own a small perf improvement (e.g., reduce p95 for short-context chat model by 10%) with clear telemetry.
- Unknowns to validate: low-level GPU kernel knowledge, familiarity with our quantization/kv-cache toolchain.

Interview score anchors (qualitative):
- Technical breadth: 7/10 (strong infra + systems, weaker on kernel catalog)
- Interview communication: 8/10 (clear + collaborative)
- Production ops: 8/10 (good migration + rollback examples)
private_notes: Keep a note: candidate mentioned a previous employer NDA — may require careful probing for code examples. Also, they asked about Redwood's approach to experimental rollouts; recommend we surface the rollouts doc in next touch.
